title: Recall Quiz: Syntax & Phrase Structure Rules

questions.q: What does the phrase structure rule S -> NP VP mean?
options: A sentence becomes a noun phrase.
A noun phrase and a verb phrase are interchangeable.
A sentence consists of a Noun Phrase and a Verb Phrase.
Syntax relies on Nouns and Verbs.
questions.explanation: It dictates the fundamental structure of an English sentence.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The cat slept', what is 'The cat'?
questions.explanation: It functions as the subject, forming a Noun Phrase (Det + N).

questions.q: A sentence that has two or more distinct underlying structural interpretations has:
questions.explanation: Structural ambiguity occurs when a sentence can be parsed in multiple ways.
A Noun Phrase centers around a noun, optionally preceded by determiners and adjectives.

questions.q: What is the head of a Verb Phrase (VP)?
questions.explanation: The head (core word) of a VP is always a verb.

questions.q: In a syntax tree, words themselves are at the:
questions.explanation: The words are the final elements, represented as leaves at the bottom of the tree.

questions.q: A Prepositional Phrase (PP) typically consists of:
questions.explanation: A preposition must be followed by its object, which is a Noun Phrase.

questions.q: What kind of grammar was developed by Noam Chomsky?
questions.explanation: TGG is Chomsky's foundational contribution to syntax.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a phrase type?
questions.explanation: While DP exists in advanced theory, standard basic PS rules focus on NP, VP, PP, AP.

questions.q: 'Flying planes can be dangerous.' This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Is the act of flying dangerous, or are the planes themselves dangerous? The structure is ambiguous.
